article_title: We spent £23,000 on fertility treatment - now our embryos will be destroyed

tasks.prompt: What legal and ethical conflict is central to the article?
options: Whether fertility clinics should provide treatment only in Wales
Whether donor consent should remain withdrawable after embryos have been created
Whether ICSI should be replaced by artificial insemination
Whether parents should be required to name children before birth
tasks.correct_answer: Whether donor consent should remain withdrawable after embryos have been created
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הכתבה עוסקת במתח בין אוטונומיית התורם לחזור בו מהסכמה לבין רצון המטופלות להשתמש בעוברים שכבר נוצרו.

tasks.prompt: Until what point can a UK sperm or egg donor withdraw consent?
options: Only before fertilisation begins
Until the child reaches one year old
Until the embryo is transferred into the womb
Only during the first month of storage
tasks.correct_answer: Until the embryo is transferred into the womb
tasks.explanation_hebrew: לפי החוק הבריטי המתואר, ניתן לבטל הסכמה עד לרגע העברת העובר לרחם.

tasks.prompt: What does “blindsided” mean when Nik describes learning about the donor's withdrawal?
options: Given unexpected and shocking news without being prepared
Unable to read the written consent form
Offered another donor immediately
Protected from emotional distress
tasks.correct_answer: Given unexpected and shocking news without being prepared
tasks.explanation_hebrew: blindsided מתאר מצב שבו אדם מופתע ונפגע מאירוע שלא היה מוכן אליו; בני הזוג לא הבינו שההסכמה יכולה להימשך בשלב זה.

tasks.prompt: What happened after Nat and Nik changed to ICSI treatment?
options: They created six embryos and Jude was later born
The clinic cancelled all treatment before fertilisation
Their donor withdrew consent before any embryos existed
They received a refund of the full £23,000
tasks.correct_answer: They created six embryos and Jude was later born
tasks.explanation_hebrew: לאחר המעבר ל־ICSI נוצרו שישה עוברים, ואחד מהם הוביל ללידת בנם Jude באוגוסט של השנה הקודמת.

tasks.prompt: Why does the withdrawal of consent intensify Sam and Carly's anxiety about their current pregnancy?
options: They have been told that Finn cannot receive medical care
They are required to end the pregnancy next year
They plan to donate all remaining embryos immediately
The stored embryos may be their only future route to parenthood if something happens to Finn
tasks.correct_answer: The stored embryos may be their only future route to parenthood if something happens to Finn
tasks.explanation_hebrew: העוברים הנותרים עומדים להיהרס, והזוג אינו בטוח שיוכל לעמוד שוב בטיפול מבחינה כלכלית, רגשית ופיזית.

tasks.prompt: What does “regulatory regime” mean in the government's response?
options: A private payment plan for fertility treatment
The system of laws and rules governing fertility treatment
A medical method for fertilising eggs
A database of all UK donors who withdrew consent
tasks.correct_answer: The system of laws and rules governing fertility treatment
tasks.explanation_hebrew: regulatory regime הוא מערך החוקים, הכללים והפיקוח המסדיר את תחום טיפולי הפוריות.

tasks.prompt: Compare the experiences of Nat and Nik Fraser-Edwards with those of Sam Beesley and Carly Estlick.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להשוות את מצב המשפחה, מספר העוברים, לוח הזמנים וההשפעה הרגשית והכלכלית על שני הזוגות.
expected_points: Nat and Nik endured failed treatment before succeeding through ICSI
They created six embryos and their son Jude was born
Their five remaining embryos will be destroyed after the donor withdrew consent
They had hoped to try for a sibling the following year
Their treatment cost £23,000 and involved loans and sacrifices
Sam and Carly are expecting their first child, Finn
Their donor also withdrew consent
Their 10 remaining embryos are due to be destroyed in 2027
They fear they may not be able to afford or endure treatment again
The news has increased anxiety during the current pregnancy

tasks.prompt: Explain the competing interests behind the current consent law and the couples' proposed change.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג באופן מאוזן את אוטונומיית התורם מול הסתמכות המטופלים על עוברים קיימים והנזק האפשרי לכל צד.
expected_points: Current law protects each donor's autonomy over whether a child may be born using their gametes
Consent can be withdrawn until transfer to the womb
After transfer, withdrawal is no longer possible
The couples invested financially and emotionally in creating embryos
They formed plans for future children based on the stored embryos
Destruction removes their possible route to genetically related siblings through those embryos
The couples want consent to become irreversible once an embryo is created
Changing the law would reduce the donor's later control
The conflict requires balancing informed consent with reliance and family-planning interests

tasks.prompt: Summarise the two couples' cases, the current law and the responses from the regulator and government.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לסכם באנגלית את העובדות המרכזיות, הכלל המשפטי, עמדת HFEA ותגובת הממשלה ללא נקיטת עמדה רפואית.
expected_points: Both couples used donor sperm and created embryos through fertility treatment
Their donors later withdrew consent
Five embryos belonging to Nat and Nik are affected
Ten embryos belonging to Sam and Carly are affected
UK law permits withdrawal until an embryo is transferred to the womb
The couples want consent to become final after embryo creation
HFEA says donor autonomy is the basis of the existing rule
HFEA cannot change the law itself
The regulator says clinics should warn patients clearly about withdrawal
The government expressed sympathy and said the regulatory regime remains under review

tasks.prompt: Write a short consultation response proposing how clinics or lawmakers should address consent withdrawal after embryos are created.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב באנגלית הצעה מאוזנת ומכבדת הכוללת הסכמה מדעת, תיעוד, זמן לבחינה ושיקולי שני הצדדים, בלי ייעוץ רפואי אישי.
expected_points: State whether the law should remain unchanged or be amended
Recognise donor autonomy
Recognise patients' emotional, financial and family-planning reliance
Require clear verbal and written explanation before treatment
Document that all parties understand the withdrawal deadline
Consider a defined cooling-off period
Explain what happens to stored embryos after withdrawal
Provide independent counselling or legal information
Collect anonymised data on how often consent is withdrawn
Include a fair review or dispute process
Use compassionate and non-judgmental language
